examPattern: Mid-Sem: 2 Hours (30 Marks) | End-Sem: 3 Hours (50 Marks) | Assignments: 20 Marks

units.title: Introduction to Cryptography & Classical Ciphers
topics: Security Goals: Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability, Non-Repudiation, Authentication
OSI Security Architecture: Attacks (Passive vs Active), Services, and Mechanisms
Classical Substitution Techniques: Caesar Cipher, Monoalphabetic, Playfair, Hill Cipher, Polyalphabetic (Vigenère)
Transposition Techniques: Rail Fence, Columnar Transposition
Steganography vs Cryptography and Cryptanalysis Techniques

units.title: Modular Arithmetic, Number Theory & Symmetric Ciphers
topics: Modular Arithmetic: Divisibility, Euclidean and Extended Euclidean Algorithms
Prime Numbers: Fermat's and Euler's Theorems, Euler's Totient Function phi(n)
Chinese Remainder Theorem and Discrete Logarithms
Feistel Cipher Structure, Simplified DES (S-DES), and Data Encryption Standard (DES)
Advanced Encryption Standard (AES): S-Box, ShiftRows, MixColumns, AddRoundKey
Block Cipher Modes of Operation: ECB, CBC, CFB, OFB, CTR

units.title: Asymmetric Cryptography, Hash Functions & Digital Signatures
topics: Public-Key Cryptography Principles and Trapdoor One-Way Functions
RSA Cryptosystem: Key Generation, Encryption, Decryption, and Security Vulnerabilities
Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange Algorithm and Man-in-the-Middle Attack
Cryptographic Hash Functions: SHA-512, MD5, and Message Authentication Codes (HMAC)
Digital Signature Standard (DSS / DSA) and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI)

textbooks: William Stallings, 'Cryptography and Network Security: Principles and Practice', 7th Edition, Pearson
Behrouz A. Forouzan, 'Cryptography and Network Security', McGraw Hill
references: Bruce Schneier, 'Applied Cryptography: Protocols, Algorithms, and Source Code in C', Wiley
Alfred J. Menezes, Paul C. van Oorschot, Scott A. Vanstone, 'Handbook of Applied Cryptography', CRC Press
